overall_assessment: Personal data is removed reliably at HiOF. Every Emneansvarlig name in the packet is gone, whether one name or two, on the label line or the line below. The packet has no e-mail addresses or phone numbers, and a scan of all 820 published hiof plans finds none either. The phone and name_like flags are false alarms: they come from ISBN and DOI digits and from reading-list authors. The remaining problems are dates. Literature-list date stamps in wordings the handler does not match are left in. The generic academic-year regexes cut digits out of URLs and remove content year ranges from references.

findings.evidence: Litteraturen er gjort tilgjengelig 13. desember 2021. … Litteraturlisten er oppdatert 16. august 2019.
findings.description: Some reading lists carry a date stamp that is left in course_plan: 'Litteratur(en) er gjort tilgjengelig <d. måned yyyy>', 'Litteraturlisten er oppdatert <d. måned yyyy>' and 'Litteraturliste oppdatert …'. The rubric counts these as administrative dates to remove, and the 'Litteraturlista er sist oppdatert …' variant is already stripped. This affects 7 of 28 packet courses (all admin_date suspects) and 19 of 820 published hiof plans. normalize_plan_text() removes only the year, so a day and month such as '13. desember' stays in the dedup hash. A new stamp on an otherwise unchanged plan can therefore create a separate plan_content_id.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: In .anon_hiof() in R/anonymize.R, the pattern (?m)^[ \t]*Litteratur\w*(?: er)? sist oppdater[^\n]* requires the words 'sist oppdater', so it misses 'er oppdatert' without 'sist' and 'er gjort tilgjengelig'. The generic date regexes in .anon_generic() catch only dd.mm.yyyy and 'd. mon. yyyy HH:MM', not a spelled-out month without a time.
findings.suggested_fix: In .anon_hiof(), change the pattern to (?m)^[ \t]*Litteratur\w*(?: er)?(?: sist)? (?:oppdater|endret|gjort tilgjengelig)[^\n]* so it also removes the whole 'Litteraturliste sist endret' line. Tested: it removes all six stamp variants and keeps 'Litteraturen er en viktig del av emnet.'. Add these cases to tests/testthat/test-anonymize.R, rebuild, and confirm the change in metrics_check.

findings.description: The academic-year pattern also matches parts of URL paths: date folders (/2019/06/, /2016/02/, /2020/03/) and numeric ids (article/view/3669/3552). It removes them and leaves broken links ('files//27/', 'uploads//NL1.2017_…', 'article/view/'). Reading-list URLs are course content, so this is content damage. It affects 3 of 28 packet courses and 20 of 820 published hiof plans, which have '//' inside a URL path. The regex is generic, so other institutions are probably affected too.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: In .anon_generic() in R/anonymize.R, the line str_remove_all("\\b\\d{4}/\\d{2,4}\\b") (academic years such as '2023/2024') has no guard against matching inside a URL or path.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the pattern so it does not match next to a slash: (?<![/\w])\d{4}/\d{2,4}\b(?!/). Tested: it leaves 'files/2019/06/27/' and 'view/3669/3552' intact and still removes 'Studieåret 2023/2024' and 'studieår 2023/24'. Another option is to apply the year regexes only outside https?://\S+ spans. Add a URL case to test-anonymize.R.

findings.evidence: Lewis, C.S. [−[1955-1956]−] [] (2001). Chronicles of Narnia … Sjette hovedrapport fra FNs klimapanel [−(2021-2022)−] … En fornyelse av Kunnskapsløftet (Meld. St. [−(2015-2016)).−] 28)
findings.description: Content year ranges in references are removed because their two years are consecutive: the first-publication years of Narnia [1955-1956], the IPCC sixth report (2021-2022), and the Storting sessions of white papers ('Meld. St. 28 (2015-2016)' becomes '(Meld. St. 28).', and 'Melding til stortinget 6 (2019–2020)' loses its session). The rubric keeps content years and document identifiers such as 'NOU 2015:2', and the session is part of a Meld. St. identifier. The Narnia removal also leaves an empty '[]' behind; that is the real cause of the artifact flag (3 published hiof plans). This affects 5 of 28 packet courses: LMUENG10417, LMUSAM11221, LMUPED10117, and LMUPED40217 and LMBPED40217 for Meld. St. 6.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: In .anon_generic(), .drop_academic_year() treats any consecutive-year range 'YYYY-YYYY+1' as an academic year, with no context check. The empty-bracket cleanup [ \t]+\([ \t]*\) handles only round brackets, so '[]' survives.
findings.suggested_fix: Exempt ranges in square brackets and ranges right after a document number: add the lookbehinds (?<!\[)(?<!(?:Meld\. St\. |St\.meld\. nr\. |Prop\. |stortinget )\d{1,3} \() to the hyphen-range pattern, and the same to the slash pattern. Tested: they keep 'Meld. St. 28 (2015-2016)', 'stortinget 6 (2019–2020)' and '[1955-1956]', and still remove 'studieåret 2023-2024'. Extend the bracket cleanup to [ \t]+[(\[][ \t]*[)\]]. An unlabelled '(2021-2022)' cannot be told apart from an academic year without context. Requiring an admin keyword (studieår, kull, gjeldende for) before such ranges is a design choice for methods.qmd.

findings.description: HiOF plans contain revision notes of the form 'dd.mm.yyyy: <what changed>'. The generic dd.mm.yyyy regex removes the date but leaves a line that starts with a stray colon. The note itself is an administrative change-log entry, not course content. Seen in 1 of 28 packet courses. In the published hiof plans there are 7 such lines, for example ': Eksamensform er endret etter vurdering av programansvarlig og studiedirektøren.' and ': Endret arbeidskrav knyttet til praksis.'.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: .anon_hiof() has no rule for dated revision notes, and in .anon_generic() the line \d{1,2}\.\d{1,2}\.\d{4} removes only the date.
findings.suggested_fix: In .anon_hiof(), before the generic pass, remove whole revision-note lines with str_remove_all("(?m)^[ \\t]*\\d{1,2}\\.\\d{1,2}\\.\\d{4}:[^\\n]*\\n?"). Add a test case.
